title: Java 8 → Latest LTS
objectives: Know the headline features of each major release
Identify the LTS versions and why they matter

sections.markdown: Since Java 9, a new feature release ships every 6 months, with a Long-Term Support (LTS) release roughly every 2–3 years (8, 11, 17, 21). Most companies target LTS versions.

rows: var in lambdas, HttpClient, single-file run
Virtual threads, record patterns, sequenced collections

sections.markdown: Know which version introduced what — a classic question. Anchor it: 8 = functional Java; 11 = first modern LTS; 17 = records/sealed; 21 = virtual threads.
Migrating off Java 8 and hitting removed/internal APIs (sun.misc.Unsafe, JAXB/Java EE modules removed in 11) and the module system. Plan dependency upgrades and run jdeps first.

flashcards.back: Lambdas, the Streams API, Optional, default methods — functional Java.
Virtual threads, record patterns, sequenced collections (all final).

quiz.explain: 8, 11, 17 and 21 are the LTS releases most teams target.
Records arrived as a standard feature in Java 16.
Project Loom's virtual threads were finalized in Java 21.

challenges.text: Convert anonymous classes to lambdas across a Java 8 codebase.
Replace verbose switches with Java 14 switch expressions and text blocks.
Refactor a DTO + visitor design to records + sealed + pattern matching (17+).
Plan and execute a Java 8 → 17 migration: run jdeps, fix removed APIs, update build.
